candidates.name: Dermatomyositis
support_spans: Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Radiographic evidence of myositis
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
candidates.why: The combination of skin manifestations, muscle inflammation, and specific autoantibodies points towards Dermatomyositis.

candidates.name: Juvenile Dermatomyositis
support_spans: A 14-year-old girl presented with a 6-year history of a photosensitive eruption
Her symptoms began at age 8 years
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
candidates.why: The patient's age and the onset of symptoms at a young age are consistent with juvenile dermatomyositis.

candidates.name: Autoimmune Disorder
support_spans: She had previously tried multiple medications including systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), with minimal improvement
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
candidates.why: The patient's lack of response to multiple immunosuppressive medications and the presence of autoantibodies suggest an underlying autoimmune disorder.

candidates.name: Scleroderma

selector.rationale: The presence of violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, and erythematous papules, along with elevated serum IFN-β levels and anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, strongly supports Dermatomyositis. The patient's history of minimal improvement with various medications also aligns with the challenging treatment of Dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While photosensitivity is a common feature, the specific skin findings and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies are more characteristic of Dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: The nailfold examination findings could suggest Scleroderma, but the overall clinical presentation and laboratory results more strongly support Dermatomyositis.
